channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Trump, Carney Optimistic on Trade Deal | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/19/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses trade negotiations between the US and Cananda. On today's show, former US Ambassador to Poland Daniel Fried, Push Digital Group Vice President T.W. Arrighi, former Obama White House Special Assistant Allison Jaslow and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Voter Registration, Data 'Not a Federal Issue,' Says Former Governor Chris Christie
item.description: Former Governor of New Jersey Chris Christie said that issues around voting registration and administering elections should be left up to states and does not see evidence from recent years that the federal government would run elections better than Governors in individual states. Christie, who is now a strategic advisor to the American Gaming Association, also weighed in on prediction market regulation and said that he is glad prediction market executives were left out of a White House meeting because they are 'illegal actors.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Minutes Show Many Officials Said Rate Hikes May Be Needed
item.description: Bloomberg's Mike McKee said that Fed minutes reflect Kevin Warsh's comment that the FOMC meeting was an 'old fashioned family fight' as members argued over inflation and the potential for a rate hike. Minutes showed that several Federal Reserve officials were in favor of an interest-rate hike last month and said that policy tightening would be necessary if inflation didn't decline. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US, Canada Said to Agree on Halving Steel, Aluminum Tariffs in Trade Talks
item.description: The tentative trade deal between the US and Canada would lower tariffs on certain Canadian exports of steel and aluminum to 25%, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Alicia Diaz

item.title: Ecuador Courts Chinese Money While Teaming Up With US Military
item.description: One of Donald Trump’s top allies in Latin America is visiting China this week, trying to secure long-term investments from the US rival.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Kueffner

item.title: Trump, Carney Optimistic on Trade Deal as Negotiators Meet in Washington
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney expressed optimism about finalizing a tariff agreement as negotiators from both countries met in Washington for further talks.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz and Tyler Kendall

item.title: California Knows What Sparks Business Innovation Says Mukunda
item.description: California is leading a group of states suing to block Paramount Skydance Corp.'s purchase of Warner Bros Discovery Inc., claiming the deal would give the combined company unfair control of movie and cable-TV businesses. Paramount executives have responded by threatening to pull its operations out of California, while Google co-founder Sergey Brin is fighting a proposed wealth tax in the state that could cost him more than $13 billion. Bloomberg Opinion Columnist, and Lecturer at Yale School of Management Gautam Mukunda joins to discuss. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: DOJ Maintains Comey Seashells Post Was Threat to Trump’s Life
item.description: The Justice Department is doubling down on its prosecution of James Comey, pushing back on the former FBI director’s assertion that a 2025 social media post wasn’t intended as a threat to President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Celine Castronuovo

item.title: Treasury Seeks to Limit Immigrants’ Use of Some Tax Breaks
item.description: The Trump administration moved to further limit immigrants’ access to the refundable portion of four tax credits aimed at aiding students, workers and families.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly

item.title: Germany Condemns Israeli Minister’s ‘Dehumanizing’ Comments
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz forcefully condemned comments by an Israeli cabinet minister, who called for nightly assassinations in Gaza despite US-led efforts to halt fighting in the war-racked Palestinian territory.
item.dc:creator: Michael Nienaber

item.title: North Korea Denies Kim Talks as Trump Seeks Meeting This Year
item.description: North Korea denied any direct communication between Kim Jong Un and President Donald Trump even as the US president said he’s seeking to meet with the strongman this year.
item.dc:creator: Se Young Lee and Tyler Kendall

item.title: Iran Risks Losing Key Economic Lifeline With UAE Halting Trade
item.description: The United Arab Emirates’ decision to cut economic ties with Iran is likely to impose more pain on the Islamic Republic as it faces the loss of a vital trade link amid escalating tensions with the US.
item.dc:creator: Golnar Motevalli

item.title: September Rate Hike Isn't Too Bad of an Idea, Bullard Says
item.description: James Bullard, former president of the St. Louis Fed and dean of Purdue's Mitch Daniels School of Business, says raising interest rates in September isn't too bad of an idea for the Federal Reserve. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy’s Woes Deepen After Graft Raid and Election Call
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s attempt to turn the page on a string of domestic setbacks backfired as the Ukrainian president fired a senior aide amid corruption allegations and faced a call for wartime elections.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova and Volodymyr Verbianyi

item.title: Poland Plans Middle-Class Tax Overhaul Ahead of Election as Bracket Creep Bites
item.description: Prime Minister Donald Tusk plans to overhaul income taxes to ease the burden on Poland’s urban middle class, moving to deliver on a campaign pledge ahead of next year’s elections, while seeking to finance the cuts with higher levies on companies.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Krasuski and Zosia Wanat

item.title: UAE Adds to Pressure on Iran After Missiles Target Territory
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has cut all economic ties with Tehran after accusing Iran of firing ballistic missiles at its territory, ramping up regional tensions.
item.dc:creator: Golnar Motevalli and Patrick Sykes

item.title: Burnham Vows ‘Huge Transfer of Power’ From Treasury to No. 10 North
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he will shift responsibility for economic growth away from the UK Treasury and toward his new office in the north of England.
item.dc:creator: Joe Mayes, Julian Harris and Ellen Milligan

item.title: Peltola’s Strength in Alaska Boosts Democratic Hopes for Senate
item.description: Mary Peltola’s strong showing in Alaska’s Senate primary is bolstering Democratic hopes that the party can defeat a two-term Republican incumbent — and possibly help it retake both houses of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Anna Edgerton and Derek Wallbank

item.title: Democratic Socialist Nixon Dominates Florida Senate Primary
item.description: Democratic Socialist Angie Nixon stormed to a surprise win in Florida’s US Senate primary, while Republican Representative Byron Donalds, backed by a $100 million war chest and President Donald Trump’s endorsement, cruised to victory in his gubernatorial primary.
item.dc:creator: Michael Smith, Daniel Cancel and Anna J Kaiser

item.title: House Epstein Panel Chair Threatens Leon Black With Contempt
item.description: The chairman of the House committee investigating Jeffrey Epstein threatened to hold Leon Black in contempt of Congress if he fails to appear before the panel next month or doesn’t produce nondisclosure agreements the panel has subpoenaed.
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Reilly and Laura Benitez
